thread:
sam: Heads-up: seeing a weird spike in GPU attach time in us-east1. Provisioning backlog ~120s and many nodes stuck 'Attaching local volume'.
anya: Oof. Any storage errors in the nodes?
devon: Yep, I pulled a quick tail from one of the stuck hosts: `dmesg` shows repeated nvme I/O timeouts + `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456` then `nvme0: multiple commands timed out`.
sam: That matches the attach failures. Also noticed attach latency correlates with a tiny subset of hosts (hot stripes?).
infra-bot: [alert] nvme-read-stall detected on gnode-usi-43. Auto-evict not triggered because device health healthy=TRUE.
michael: I ran `fio --name=readtest --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=8` on one affected host and it shows large read latency tail: p99 ~ 1.2s, avg ~ 80ms. Other healthy nodes p99 < 10ms.
anya: Sounds like read-head stalls causing huge tail latencies. Could be firmware or thermal throttling? Any SMART flags?
devon: SMART looks normal except occasional `Media and Data Integrity Errors: 1` on the host. But SMART counters are noisy; not definitive.
ops-oncall: Customer-facing impact? We had ~15 GPU allocation retries in past 30m, fallbacks triggered to us-west2. No major customer reports yet but metric alert fired.
sam: Immediate mitigation: switch new jobs to prefer us-west2 for next 30m and drain unaffected hosts in us-east1 when they finish current jobs. Also reduced batch size on scheduler to avoid heavy random reads.
anya: I'll open a maintenance job to repro with longer fio runs and kernel tracing. Can someone grab `perf record -e block:block_rq_issue` during a stall?
devon: On it. Also capturing nvme tracepoints: `trace-cmd record -e nvme* -a`.
infra-bot: [note] Provisioner: set region preference rule -> prefer: us-west2; duration: 30m.
michael: Short-term patch: increase janitor delay before starting aggressive cleanup tasks on ephemeral disks (we suspect the cleaner overlaps with heavy workload causing head collisions). I bumped the janitor window for the affected host pool by +10m.
anya: Interesting—cleaner overlap would explain correlation with batch job window. Did we see scrub/sweep tasks around the same timestamps?
devon: Yes, cron-scrub logs show scrub start at 03:12 which lines up with first attach timeouts.
sam: Plan of record: (1) keep routing away from the pool until we confirm stability, (2) run extended fio + nvme trace to reproduce, (3) test vendor firmware suggested patch on a canary host, (4) tune janitor overlap rules to avoid active GPU attach windows, (5) add an automatic small-IO probe to detect read-head stalls earlier.
ops-oncall: Can we add a soft-evict if read p99 > 500ms for > 2m? That would free up attaches.
devon: We can — I'll PR a short-circuit that flags nodes with sustained high randread p99 for probe eviction.
anya: For the canary firmware test, we should also check power/thermal telemetry. Some hosts show repeated fan RPM dips at the same times.
michael: Noted. Also cross-check NVMe vendor logs for queued async events.
sam: Cost note — moving to us-west2 and extra retries will increase cross-region egress and provisioning churn. Keep finance in the loop if this persists.
infra-bot: [action] created issue INF-9241: "us-east1 local-nvme read-head stall investigation" assigned to devon, anya.
ops-oncall: I'll keep on-call routing updated and post if customer errors escalate.
devon: Quick repro data: attached fio profile (summary): throughput 80MB/s, iops 20k, p50 2ms p95 120ms p99 1.1s, 50% of nvme cmd timeouts during random read phase.
anya: After bumping janitor window and shifting jobs, attach latency dropped to ~20s and backlog cleared over ~12min. We're still monitoring.
michael: If firmware fix looks promising, plan to schedule phased update with 5% canary then 25% then full region.
sam: Good. After stability window (1h) we'll close INF-9241 and document mitigation (janitor windows + small-IO probe + firmware rollout plan).
ops-oncall: I'll update the incident channel if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
devon: Leaving traces and fio outputs in the incident ticket. Will follow up with PR for auto-evict rule.
anya: Thanks team. If it reoccurs, we'll capture a full `blktrace` on one of the nodes.
sam: End of thread: follow-up in INF-9241 and incident check in 1h.
